about: Each requirement of the public readiness specification, split into parts with an honest status for the current product. A status is a judgement recorded here; the traceability check verifies its form, its evidence links and its consistency, not that the judgement is right.

requirements.summary: Chemical graph, scene, containment and external references live in separate namespaces and are compared separately.

parts.summary: Chemical graph and scene positions are held and compared separately.
One ordered scene tree holds groups and simple graphics; scene-owned directed references separately name objects, atoms or bonds without chemical semantics.

Multiple chemical graphs/pages, specialized scene objects beyond implemented independent captions and simple graphics, and reaction/style references beyond generic directed links remain unsupported. Open follow-ups are P36 for advanced graphic scene types, P37 for geometric object references, P40 for multiple pages, P49 for persistent reaction-role/mapping references, and the existing optional S05 for collaborative reference invariants. Bounded P35 caption/display editing is delivered and is no longer an unfinished follow-up; this does not claim the broader multi-graph model is complete.

requirements.summary: Atoms carry element, isotope, charge, hydrogen, radical and query information, each compared atom by atom.

parts.summary: Atoms record an element symbol (1-118), a formal charge in -8..8 and an optional isotope mass number 1..999 as drawn; values outside these ranges are refused and change nothing.
Hydrogen states are recorded and told apart as drawn: stated with a count of 0 to 16, unknown, or inferred (the default). Inferred counts are separate read-only interpretations.

Radicals (singlet, doublet, triplet, unknown), query atoms (any, any but hydrogen, heteroatom, halogen, or a list of 1 to 10 elements, optionally negated), query bonds (any, or a list of single, double, triple and aromatic), aromatic, dative and unknown bonds, and attachment points 1 to 4 are recorded, refused in invalid combinations with a stable reason, saved, reopened and undone. Recording is separate from the bounded aromaticity interpretation; matching is MODEL-02.7.
A bounded named valence policy reports additional hydrogens and uncertain states without changing the drawing.
A named bounded policy interprets cyclic systems and converts supported aromatic and Kekule representations without changing the input during inspection.
A bounded versioned graph identity reports canonical numbering, symmetry and supported recorded or normalized comparisons without editing either snapshot.

A bounded substructure search of one drawing in another returns every atom and bond mapping under a named model, compares query atoms, query bonds, stated charge and isotope, reads aromatic and Kekule spellings alike through the aromaticity model, and refuses what it cannot read or finish instead of answering empty.
Broader valence and aromaticity models, additional fused and charged systems, and query matching.

requirements.summary: Drawn stereo marks, chemical configuration, CIP labels and enhanced stereo groups are kept apart.

parts.summary: Drawn stereo marks (wedge and hash on single bonds with the narrow end recorded in the mark, wavy on single bonds, crossed on double bonds) and stated configurations (tetrahedral centers with three or four bonded neighbors, double bonds, and an explicit unknown) are stored apart from each other, set and cleared by three commands, refused with stable reasons, cleared with a neighbor change and reported in the reply, and kept through undo, redo, save and reopen. Statements only: these commands label nothing, check nothing against the drawing and compare nothing (reading a configuration off the drawing is MODEL-03.2, comparing it with the drawing is MODEL-03.3), and the commands themselves are not drawn (the web editor's mark gestures are MODEL-03.4).

Derivation of a configuration from a drawing: set_configuration_from_drawing stores the center or double-bond state that wedge, hash, wavy and crossed marks and one scene instance's positions show, on request only, idempotently and as one undo step, replacing the stored record of every item it processes (a configuration stated by hand and an unknown included) and writing nothing for an item it skips, or refuses with one of six stereo_not_derivable_* reasons. The rules (frame, sign, fourth position, scope) are Chemifree choices named chemifree-stereo-1; the pure rules for the mirror image, the flip and a changed neighbor order (mirrored, flipped_over, turn_for_order) are defined and tested. Nothing judges whether an atom is stereogenic or computes a CIP label, the command itself reports no disagreement (it overwrites the statement of what it processes; the comparison is MODEL-03.3), and no mirror or flip command exists.

Consistency inspection: the read-only operation chem.stereo (chemifree-stereo-1, separate from chem.validate, which stays valence-only) compares each stored configuration with what each scene instance's drawing shows, per center and double bond that is stored or marked, as agrees, disagrees, only_stored, only_drawn or neither, with a structured label_differs field for the one non-atom position, a stereogenicity_assessed false marker and closed advisory diagnostics (drawing_disagrees, drawing_not_derivable, marks_without_configuration, configuration_without_marks, mark_narrow_end_not_a_center, center_has_aromatic_bond, double_bond_substituents_same_side, wavy_between_possible_centers, drawing_weak_evidence, stereo_not_checked). It stores, derives and edits nothing, is bounded at 20,000 entries (resource_limit naming instance), judges no stereogenicity, computes no CIP label and checks no ring or strain plausibility; chem.identity and chem.substructure still do not read stereo; the web editor's indicator is MODEL-03.5.

Drawn stereo marks in the web editor: the bond-kind group draws wedge, hashed wedge and wavy marks (crossed is set and shown through the bond inspector), a drag or click makes the bond, its mark and the configuration the drawing then shows in one transaction (one undo step) with the narrow end where the gesture started, the click cycle, order changes and the inspector clear the mark or stored double-bond configuration an edit would otherwise be refused for, a configuration the service will not derive leaves the mark in place with the reason shown, and a status line tells what a gesture stored, replaced or removed. Rendering constants are stand-ins for the public BoldWidth and HashSpacing document settings and every other geometry is a Chemifree choice. Comparing a stored configuration with the drawing is MODEL-03.5; the editor has no mirror or flip, no crossed canvas tool, and does not update a stored configuration when atoms move. The browser smoke exercises the same gestures but is not an evidence check of this record.

Agreement indicator in the web editor: for a drawing that holds a mark or a stored configuration the page calls chem.stereo on its own (300 ms after the last change, one request in flight and one more for changes made meanwhile, none while dragging, none for a drawing without stereo) and uses a reply only when it is for exactly the drawing on screen, positions included (otherwise Checking the drawing... with aria-busy and no ring). The reply is validated strictly against its snapshot and refused as a whole on any mismatch; the outcome must be ok with chemifree-stereo-1. The result is a summary line, a Stereo panel row per item and placement, and a ring on the canvas for each item that does not agree (solid for a disagreement, dashed for a state with nothing to compare, named, no pointer events), with a switch that turns the automatic check off (Check now asks once) and one-click edits built from the latest document: Update from drawing and Store from drawing (set_configuration_from_drawing), Remove stored (null) and Update all from drawing, each one undo step with a status line naming the replaced or removed value. Only stored configurations are compared with the drawing: the comparison itself judges no atom stereogenic and computes no CIP label (not assessed, never worded as no stereo; CIP labels are MODEL-03.7). A stored configuration is never changed except by the user's click, and moving atoms still does not update one. The browser smoke exercises the indicator, the ring and the one-click edits in a real browser but is not an evidence check of this record.

CIP labels: the read-only operation chem.cip (chemifree-cip-1) computes R or S for stored tetrahedral centers and E or Z for stored double bonds from the current graph, on demand and never stored, by Rules 1a, 1b, 2 and 3 only (duplicate and phantom atoms, implicit hydrogens, mancude all-carbon aromatic rings). Every item has an explicit state: assigned, none, unspecified, unknown, ambiguous or unsupported with a reason from a closed list, and the outcome is partial with a loss entry for each ambiguous or unsupported item. A CipLabeler port with a built-in labeler whose answers the application validates; scope stored, stereogenic or named items; bounded by 20,000 digraph nodes per item and 2,000,000 per request (resource_limit), with no time limit (a documented gap). Rules 4a to 5, pseudoasymmetric r and s, heteroaromatic rings and axes or planes are not applied and a tie they might break is unsupported, never none; no claim of equivalence with any other program, and a manual one-version RDKit comparison is evidence only. The web editor shows them only behind two switches that are off by default (MODEL-03.7).

CIP labels in the web editor: two Stereo panel switches, Atom stereo labels and Bond stereo labels (off by default, not saved), are the only thing that makes the page ask chem.cip, and only with scope stored (never stereogenic, because the operation has no time limit), scheduled like the agreement check (300 ms after the last committed change, one request in flight, none while dragging). A reply is read by a validator that checks every required field and value and ignores fields it does not know (state, descriptor and reason pairing; four ranked positions that are the item's own; E or Z only on bonds and R or S only on atoms; the stored record, snapshot, model, rules, scope, diagnostics and loss entries must fit) and is shown only for exactly the drawing on screen; any mismatch (an unlisted stored item included; a well-formed diagnostic code it does not know is only kept), a limit or another error shows CIP labels unavailable with the service's message and no label. Only an assigned item gets overlay text on the canvas ((S) near a center, (E) near a double bond; text form and placement are Chemifree choices, not legacy behavior), as an overlay that is not part of the document or an export; each Stereo row with a stored configuration gets a CIP cell under the switch of its kind (label, none, unknown, ambiguous or not supported with the reason sentence, or not examined) next to the agreement with the drawing. A label describes the stored configuration, never the drawing, is never written to the document and touches no mark; no enhanced-group meaning is implied. The client check runs the validator, the view and scheduler rules and mutation checks of them; the browser smoke exercises the switches, the overlay, the panel cell, the refusal state and an unchanged document in a real browser but is not an evidence check of this record.

Enhanced stereo groups in the document: absolute, and and or groups over stored tetrahedral centers, with the number kept as stated (0, negative and omitted included; an omitted number reads as 0), the interpreted number and a display label computed and never stored, one absolute group per document, created and changed by eight commands in document.transaction (required keys, group and atom references, 12 stereo_group_* reasons with the command index, a 32-bit number range), listed in every snapshot as stereo.groups, left by a member whose configuration goes, followed by undo and redo with stable ids, saved and reopened, and reported in notes (partial) when an edit changes which centers are stated to belong together. Statements only: no ratio is stated for and, nothing judges that members are related or stereogenic, chem.cip, chem.identity, chem.substructure and chem.validate ignore groups, and chem.stereo says it does not examine them. The web editor's display and editing of groups is STEREO-01.2.
CIP Rules 4a to 5 with pseudoasymmetric r and s, heteroaromatic rings and axes or planes, isotope-aware and symmetry-aware stereo, mirror and flip commands, and a crossed-mark canvas tool.

requirements.summary: Advanced objects (tables, TLC plates, plasmids, polymers, images) keep their hierarchy, references, text and style.

parts.summary: All of this requirement: nothing of it is implemented.

requirements.summary: An XML document format is read and written with typed styles, ids and text, reporting what is lost.

parts.summary: Bounded CDXML rich read/write of ordered pages, graphs, styles, Unicode text, IDs and known references, with a consented loss-accounted single-graph editor projection. P33h explicitly copies consented whole-drawing first-placement CDXML text with manual fallback. P33i reads/manual-enters exact CDXML UTF-8 text (120KiB), then explicitly selects page/molecule and previews/accepts losses before creating a new drawing; it does not append or edit the current graph. Uncertain creation retains the original request/source/digest/process and Saved-documents reconciliation after restart. CDX remains binary download, without clipboard base64 text. Bounded P33 is recorded as done against the roadmap scope and acceptance criteria. Implementation head 7e7c921fae0ce2e4f3e6f5ff8222ca2859698dca passed isolated npm run check, the standard browser smoke and all eight clipboard browser commands; PR #172 CI check/browser passed. Merge 1082293 post-merge main CI check/browser also passed (https://github.com/EunhakChoi/chemifree/actions/runs/42149543576); this documentation PR still requires final review dispositions and current-head CI. Evidence and limits: docs/verification/p33-clipboard-completion.md.

CDXML stereo import (P29b), from what the public sources confirm: bond Display values (wedge and hashed wedge with the narrow end at B for ...Begin and at E for ...End, wavy; Solid plain; Bold, Dash, Dot and DashDot as plain bonds with a no-consent note; Wavy on a double bond the crossed mark; Hash, HollowWedge*, WavyWedge* and any mark on a non-single bond or in Display2 imported plain with a consent-required stereo_mark_unplaceable loss; any other value refused), the atom Geometry, BondOrdering and AS hints noted and never stored, configurations derived from the marks and positions as the MOL import does (a center that does not derive keeps its mark and reports stereo_unreadable), and EnhancedStereoType with EnhancedStereoGroupNum (any 32-bit integer, omitted as 0, Or 1 and And 1 separate, Or 2 and Or 258 two groups) mapped to P27 groups in the same transaction, a member that is no derived tetrahedral center refusing the file. Double-bond E/Z is not derived, CIP labels are never stored, DoublePosition and a bond CIP attribute stay refused, The P29e bounded drawing export writes confirmed marks and enhanced groups with per-loss digest consent; no marks or CIP labels are synthesized. P29f exposes the same bounded drawing export in the web panel: explicit digest consent before download, complete snapshot/format/service-generation freshness, download revalidation and decoded binary CDX; codec semantics are unchanged. P29g adds named normalization/roundtrip and exact-consent conformance cases plus separate graph/configuration/partition/mark corpus checks; group-indicator visibility is explicit normalized output (0445), never claimed retained.
Advanced CDXML objects, editor rendering and full-format interoperability remain open.

requirements.summary: A binary document format is framed with bounded lengths, nesting and references, reporting what is lost.

parts.summary: For the bounded CDX subset, the header, tagged objects and properties, 0xFFFF extended lengths, nesting, strings and references are read and written with limits enforced before allocation, byte offsets on errors and a loss report.

CDX stereo import (P29b): atom tags and the bond Display 0601 (INT16 0 to 14, one table with CDXML). Geometry 0430 (one byte, 7 tetrahedral), BondOrdering 0431 (32-bit entries, no count), CIP 0437 (INT8 0 to 6, a hint never stored), EnhancedStereoType 0446 (one byte) and EnhancedStereoGroupNum 0447 (two bytes little-endian read as unsigned 16-bit, so 128 and 258 stay as written) are read through the same projection as CDXML. The tags of Display2 and DoublePosition and of the atom label are not in the public sources used, so a bond that carries them is refused as before; an atom with an enhanced stereo type in a fragment with no readable mark has nothing to derive a center from, so the file is refused rather than guessed. P29e adds bounded drawing export of marks and groups whose output drawing derives every stored member; unknown carriers retain strict opaque preservation. P29f exposes the same bounded drawing export in the web panel: explicit digest consent before download, complete snapshot/format/service-generation freshness, download revalidation and decoded binary CDX; codec semantics are unchanged. P29g adds named normalization/roundtrip and exact-consent conformance cases plus separate graph/configuration/partition/mark corpus checks; group-indicator visibility is explicit normalized output (0445), never claimed retained.
Other binary formats, and CDX content beyond the bounded subset, remain open.

requirements.summary: MOL V2000/V3000 and SDF are read and written with query and stereo fields, reporting per-field loss.

parts.summary: Bounded V2000 MOL/SDF element graph and SD data conversion, with atomic preview/import and source-index maps. Query, stereo and V3000 remain outside this part.

Provider-level V3000 connection-table core: logical-line reader with continuation, block parser, a core-subset writer (element atoms, bonds 1-4, charge, isotope, radical) and closed refusal reasons. It is reached through the operations by CODEC-03.v3000-wire; query, SGroup, stereo and collection meaning are outside this part.

MOL/SDF import and export of the V3000 core subset through document.import and document.export: record dialect detection, aromatic bonds, bond marks (wedge, hash, wavy, crossed) both ways with the configurations they show derived on import, the ctab request key (v2000 default, v3000, auto), V2000 bond stereo column writing and reading (wedge, hash, either), and accepted_losses consent for stereo a file cannot carry. Query atoms and bonds, dative bonds, SGroups, R-groups, remain outside this part; the stereo collections are CODEC-03.v3000-groups and the web choice is CODEC-03.v3000-web.

V3000 COLLECTION blocks and the P27 enhanced stereo groups, both ways: STEABS, STERAC<n> and STEREL<n> written with the group's interpreted number as stated (omitted as 0, any 32-bit integer), the chiral flag written as 1 only when an absolute group exists (a product rule), the consent loss stereo_ungrouped_centers for stored centers in no group, the informational stereo_group_identity, import in the same transaction with closed refusals (empty, duplicate, shared atom, member that is not a stored tetrahedral center, out-of-range atom), renumbering of a colliding number and joining of the absolute group on append with reported losses, and the mol-v2000 and mol-v3000 format ids. V2000 carries no groups, CDX reads them, and recorded CXSMILES reads and writes supported groups; SGroups, query atoms and bonds, dative bonds remain outside this part; the web choice is CODEC-03.v3000-web.

The web MOL and SDF panel over the V3000 operations: a version control (V2000 default, V3000, Auto) sent as the ctab key and held by the page only, the written dialect shown from result.ctab, the export consent step (losses listed with plain sentences, an explicit accept, accepted_losses with the digest, a changed digest asks again), and one plain sentence per closed V3000 refusal reason with a generic fallback for the rest, checked against the reason table in the contract. The Stereo panel note is true of this build: V3000 export writes groups, V2000 and SMILES carry none. No query, SGroup or R-group support is claimed; those files are refused. P33d adds explicit MOL-text export after existing V2000/V3000/Auto loss consent and manual fallback; explicit read/manual text goes to the service only on Preview, with exact source/destination/process/digest consent before single-placement append. It preserves existing coordinates, live selection and history, without native offsets/automatic target selection. Same-request uncertain import and restart reconciliation apply. Bounded P33 is recorded as done against the roadmap scope and acceptance criteria. Implementation head 7e7c921fae0ce2e4f3e6f5ff8222ca2859698dca passed isolated npm run check, the standard browser smoke and all eight clipboard browser commands; PR #172 CI check/browser passed. Merge 1082293 post-merge main CI check/browser also passed (https://github.com/EunhakChoi/chemifree/actions/runs/42149543576); this documentation PR still requires final review dispositions and current-head CI. Evidence and limits: docs/verification/p33-clipboard-completion.md.
V3000 query atoms and bonds, dative bonds, SGroups, R-groups and advanced MOL/SDF features remain open.

requirements.summary: Reaction formats keep reactant, product and agent roles, steps and mapping independent of layout.

parts.summary: All of this requirement: nothing of it is implemented.

requirements.summary: Line notations (SMILES, InChI) are interpreted, distinguishing string equality from chemical equality and reporting loss.

parts.summary: Bounded OpenSMILES subset: branches, ring labels, dot-disconnected parts, isotopes, charges, hydrogens and aromatic atoms are read; recorded-order and Chemifree-canonical text is written. Invalid text is refused with its position and a specific code; every written string is read back by the same reader. The canonical form is Chemifree's own (chemifree-smiles-canonical-1, bound to chemifree-chemical-graph-2), not another toolkit's. Recorded output writes supported tetrahedral stereo and CXSMILES groups; canonical output reports stereo losses. The stereo read is CODEC-05.smiles-stereo-read; query and reaction SMILES and InChI import remain open. P33g adds explicit SMILES clipboard reading into the source field and direct prepared whole-graph output copying/manual fallback. Existing grammar,16KiB UTF-8 limit, recorded/canonical loss-consent and generated-grid single-placement append remain; immutable same-request/process uncertainty and restart reconciliation cover typed and clipboard commits. No format guessing,external Cut or shortcuts. Bounded P33 is recorded as done against the roadmap scope and acceptance criteria. Implementation head 7e7c921fae0ce2e4f3e6f5ff8222ca2859698dca passed isolated npm run check, the standard browser smoke and all eight clipboard browser commands; PR #172 CI check/browser passed. Merge 1082293 post-merge main CI check/browser also passed (https://github.com/EunhakChoi/chemifree/actions/runs/42149543576); this documentation PR still requires final review dispositions and current-head CI. Evidence and limits: docs/verification/p33-clipboard-completion.md.

SMILES tetrahedral marks @ and @@ of bracket atoms are read as stored configurations with no bond mark (neighbour order after OpenSMILES: preceding atom, bracket hydrogen, ring labels in the order written, then branches and chain), in the same transaction as the atoms; marks the drawing cannot hold (a lone pair as the fourth position, an aromatic atom, other neighbour counts, a charged or hypervalent atom), the @TH, @AL, @SP, @TB and @OH classes and the directional bonds / and \ are refused with a code, a closed diagnostic family and the span, never dropped. Checked by hand-worked neighbour orders, respellings giving one configuration, and a hand-run RDKit comparison of CIP labels (RDKit 2026.09.1). Recorded output also writes supported stereo; this part records the reader evidence.

Optional Linux Standard InChI/InChIKey generation via chem.inchi and an explicitly registered public 1.07.5 library. Declared version, checked SHA-256, effective finite cooperative timeout, stored 0D tetrahedral/double-bond stereo, refusal of unsupported graph and AND/OR groups, loss-bound consent for omitted marks/absolute group metadata and opaque native warnings, and honest unavailable states. Native boundaries 10/10, six direct native and four application/provider exact comparisons with the separately executed official 1.07.5 executable passed (same distribution, not an independent chemical engine). Consent tests 6/6, CLI configuration integration 7/7 and API/CLI configuration modules 4/4 each passed; full local checks, browser smoke and merged-main check/browser CI passed. Codex and independent subagent findings were fixed with regressions (PR #149). Official comparisons are local opt-in evidence from the same distribution; ordinary CI does not run them. This closes only the bounded Linux generator profile. No InChI import, web panel or complete stereo/equality claim.

Unsupported stereo writing, the directional bonds / and \ on read, the @TH, @AL, @SP, @TB and @OH classes and every CXSMILES field other than the three stereo group fields, query SMILES, reaction SMILES, InChI import and other line notations remain open. Directional bond reading/writing is the explicitly deferred P29c2 scope; lone-pair fourth-position SMILES marks remain refused. InChI import and dedicated UI remain unsupported and are outside the completed bounded generator; broader text import/export UX is tracked by P48.

requirements.summary: Unknown objects and properties are preserved, refused or reported according to a stated policy.

parts.summary: For the bounded V2000 profile, unsupported chemical directives are refused and projection, metadata and interpretation losses are reported.
For bounded CDXML, unchanged opaque content is preserved; unsafe edits require explicit discard, and uninterpreted selected chemistry is refused.

For bounded CDX, unknown objects and properties stay opaque binary, an unchanged original is returned byte for byte, edits need an explicit discard, and content with no CDX encoding is dropped or rounded only with reported consent.

For bounded SMILES, syntax the drawing cannot hold (unsupported stereo, wildcard, quadruple bonds, extended ring labels, charges and isotopes outside the drawing's range, aromatic systems outside the aromaticity model) is refused with its own code and position; dropped text, atom classes and undetermined radicals are reported as losses that need acceptance.

Advanced unknown/unsupported objects and format interoperability beyond the implemented codecs and bounded P33 clipboard profiles remain open. Existing codec/export rows cover their declared advanced objects; P48 covers integrated file/drop/text import/export UX and W04 covers Windows metafile output. Native instance/enhanced-group cloning, custom MIME and external-app clipboard compatibility are not newly promised by removing completed P33 from this catch-all.

requirements.summary: Selections and containment determine exactly which objects a move, delete or clean-up affects.

parts.summary: Deleting atoms deletes exactly the bonds that touch them, and undo restores both.
Sibling graphics can be grouped; moving a selected group and child applies once and undo/redo restores selection.

Delivered bounded P31 web-only viewport separates navigation from document edits and selection: per-tab/canvas center and scale, keyboard and mouse pan/anchored zoom/fit/reset, one-pointer Pan view touch, inverse SVG coordinates, 3 CSS-pixel drag threshold and scale-adjusted hit testing. Navigation sends no commands, changes no revision/undo/dirty/saved coordinates, preserves the view across edits and resize, and resets on document identity/reload. No pinch or multi-touch. PR #150 merged; final local checks and merged-main check/browser CI passed.

Bounded P32a read-only document.selection_scope and atomic move_selection resolve the deterministic union of selected scene subtrees, atom positions and bond endpoints in the selected placement. Overlaps move once, references/connectivity are not followed, other placements and chemistry stay, invalid targets/coordinate overflow roll back the transaction, and empty/zero movement preserves revision/history/redo. The movement selection is independent of history selection_before/after. Both dedicated conformance cases passed in clean isolated suite28. P32a initially introduced server-only scope/movement; P32b/P32c add arrangement/transform primitives and P32d–f provide the verified bounded web controls. Bounded P32 implementation delivery, reviews and PR/main CI are complete as recorded in docs/verification/p32-selection-completion.md; this completion documentation PR still awaits its own review/CI.

Bounded P32b geometry-only document.arrangement_plan and atomic arrange_objects: six union-bound alignments and horizontal/vertical equal-edge-gap distribution of outermost scene units. Descendants of selected ancestors are absorbed into rigid groups, leading-edge/ID order is deterministic, endpoints stay fixed, and too few units, empty geometry, negative gap, coordinate overflow or a rounded center plan that would move again on repetition (arrangement_center_unstable) refuse whole. Center midpoint ties retain equally close poses; genuine one-ULP improvements are preserved. No-op preserves history/redo; plans include original bounds/nominal deltas/translation anchors/scopes and exact snapshot, not a commit token. Anchors reconstruct each moved coordinate with exact coordinate + target - source summed before one binary64 ties-even rounding; null leaves stationary units untouched. Both dedicated conformance cases passed in clean isolated suite28. P32b initially introduced server primitives; P32d provides verified bounded whole-object web alignment/distribution, while P32c and P32f add shared and mixed web transforms. Partial atom arrangement and snapping remain absent. Bounded P32 implementation delivery, reviews and PR/main CI are complete as recorded in docs/verification/p32-selection-completion.md; this completion documentation PR still awaits its own review/CI.

Bounded P32c document.transform_plan and atomic transform_selection use the existing exact selected union and explicit finite pivot for geometry-only rotation and horizontal/vertical axis reflection. Positive degrees are clockwise in page coordinates; modulo-360 identities and quarter turns avoid trigonometric drift. Arbitrary rotations support atoms, lines and arrows; any selected rectangle, including descendants/degenerate rectangles, requires an exact quarter turn. Plans report immutable snapshot/scope and exact before/after geometry; drawing_stereo_may_change is only an advisory that graph positions change, not a stereo assessment or loss. Hierarchy, references, marks, stored configurations/groups and other placements remain unchanged; invalid/unsupported/out-of-range targets roll back the whole edit. Empty/identity no-op preserves revision/history/redo. Both dedicated conformance cases passed in clean isolated suite28. P32c initially introduced the explicit-pivot server primitive; P32d and P32f provide verified bounded center-pivot web controls for scene and mixed selections. The server still requires an explicit pivot; diagonal reflection, snapping and cleanup remain absent. Bounded P32 implementation delivery, reviews and PR/main CI are complete as recorded in docs/verification/p32-selection-completion.md; this completion documentation PR still awaits its own review/CI.

P32d bounded web Scene controls expose six geometry-bound alignments, two equal-edge-gap distributions, clockwise/counterclockwise quarter-turn rotation and horizontal/vertical axis reflection for whole scene objects. Selected ancestor/descendant units collapse once; rotation/reflection submits an explicit pivot at the current selected geometry-bounds center. Bounds exclude labels/strokes. At P32d introduction all geometry controls excluded explicit atom/bond targets; P32f supersedes that restriction for the four transform buttons, while alignment/distribution remain disabled for partial graph targets; missing targets lapse as a whole, empty geometry and insufficient arrangement units are gated, and queued actions recompute against the latest document while retaining the selection captured at press. Sibling grouping preserves independent atom/bond selection and replaces grouped member selection with the created group without discarding unrelated live choices. Existing authoritative server validation, history and stored-stereo limits remain; P32d itself has no arbitrary-angle/custom-pivot/diagonal-reflection UI; mixed selection transforms are tracked separately as P32f. Bounded mixed canvas selection/movement is tracked separately as P32e; snapping and cleanup remain absent. Final implementation eeb6f7a passed isolated npm run check (373 client,105 conformance), strict routes (0/1000 stalled) and no-skips browser (skipped_steps=[], both mixed-selection result flags true). Bounded P32 is delivered through PR #161 merge 2c7a518 with successful PR/main CI; this completion documentation PR CI remains pending. Scope limits and all review/finding dispositions are recorded in docs/verification/p32-selection-completion.md.

P32e bounded mixed canvas selection/movement adds Shift-click atom/bond/graphic toggles and inclusive empty-canvas marquee selection of active-placement atom centers plus graphics whose two defining points are fully contained; Shift-marquee adds, and bonds/groups/whole placements are not implicitly box-selected. A captured mixed scene/atom/bond selection previews deduplicated per-placement geometry and submits one existing move_selection union command. The visible active movement placement is distinct from the shared graph: changing it clears atom/bond selection but retains scene-object choices; a missing placement never silently falls back to a remaining one. Captured targets/placement are revalidated when queued, and an expired reference lapses the whole action. Existing transaction selection/history/replay and authoritative server bounds remain; no backend/operation/catalog/scientific behavior changes. At P32e introduction transform buttons remained scene-object-only; P32f supersedes that restriction for quarter turns and reflections. Alignment/distribution still accept only whole scene objects. Final implementation eeb6f7a passed isolated npm run check (373 client,105 conformance), strict routes (0/1000 stalled) and no-skips browser (skipped_steps=[], both mixed-selection result flags true). Bounded P32 is delivered through PR #161 merge 2c7a518 with successful PR/main CI; this completion documentation PR CI remains pending. Scope limits and all review/finding dispositions are recorded in docs/verification/p32-selection-completion.md.

P32f bounded web quarter-turn and horizontal/vertical axis-reflection buttons transform a captured mixed scene/atom/bond selection with one existing transform_selection command. parts.summary: A transaction applies all its commands or none; a refused transaction names the failing command index and leaves revision, content and history unchanged.
Each changing transaction, undo and redo adds one revision; a transaction that changes nothing adds none; an edit after undo drops the redo branch without reusing atom ids.
A write based on a stale revision is refused with the current revision and changes nothing, including an aromaticity conversion whose revision became stale while it computed.

Saved content and history survive a crash; edits neither saved nor drafted do not; an autosaved draft is recovered with its history; closing does not discard unsaved work without the confirmed revision.

Adding, moving and deleting scene instances, moving atoms within one instance, and the positions a new or deleted atom has in every instance are one change set with the graph changes: one revision per effective change, none for a no-op, undone and redone as a whole; refused commands change nothing.
Scene creation, grouping, ordering, translation, references and selection are atomic and restored together by undo and redo; deletion rejects surviving dangling references.

requirements.summary: Stereo group labels, partitions and omissions are handled per format.

parts.summary: Group labels, partitions and omissions, in the editor and for the documented bounded export profiles: a group keeps its identifier and members apart from the stored number, the interpreted number and the display label (stored and shown in snapshots, 0, negative and omitted numbers as stated, Or 1 and And 1 distinct, one absolute group, singleton groups legal); renumbering and adding members are not losses, while splitting, merging, removing members and a member losing its configuration are reported; recorded SMILES writes supported groups and reports consent loss for groups it cannot write, canonical SMILES and V2000 MOL exports need consent to drop groups (a V3000 export writes them, see CODEC-03.v3000-groups), and CIP and identity ignore groups. CDXML and CDX preserve readable groups with the documented loss and numbering rules.

Enhanced stereo groups are read from CDXML (and from the CDX atom tags, for atoms whose marks are available): same kind and number is one group, Or 1 and And 1 stay separate, an omitted number is read as 0 and joins a stated 0, Absolute carries no number, negative and large numbers stay as stated, CDX group numbers are unsigned 16-bit; a member that is not a derived tetrahedral center refuses the file and nothing is created. P29e drawing export writes a group only when all members derive from the written drawing, otherwise reports the whole omitted group for consent; output numbers outside 1–127 are normalized per kind without merging, and native IDs have informational losses. The CXSMILES groups are STEREO-01.cxsmiles-groups-read. P29g adds named normalization/roundtrip and exact-consent conformance cases plus separate graph/configuration/partition/mark corpus checks; group-indicator visibility is explicit normalized output (0445), never claimed retained.

Stereo groups are shown and edited in the web editor: the Stereo panel's Group cell and group list read only from the snapshot (id, label, kind, the stored number as stated against the interpreted one, member count, member chips), one-click make absolute, group as AND or OR, add, remove, merge, split, set number and delete on the selected atoms in one transaction each (enabled only when the contract's preconditions hold, a disabled control saying why in text), a plain sentence for each of the twelve stereo_group refusal reasons, the reply's notes shown as for other stereo notes, and a Group labels canvas overlay that is off by default, not saved and never part of the document. The page states that its recorded SMILES and V3000 exports write supported groups, while canonical SMILES and V2000 report omitted groups, that groups are not compared with the drawing and do not change CIP labels or identity, and claims no ratio for any kind. Nothing here maps groups to any file format.

The CXSMILES fields a:, o<n>: and &<n>: after a SMILES text are read as enhanced stereo groups over the tagged centers (0-based atom indexes in the order atoms are written, the digits after o or & stored as the group number, same kind and number one group, a number-less o: or &: refused); every other field, a malformed block, an index that is no atom, no @ or @@ center, or listed twice is refused with its span and nothing is imported. A tagged center in no group states nothing. The groups map through the same group commands as V3000 and CDXML. Field syntax rests on the public RDKit Book examples, not on the functional specification, which has no CXSMILES; P29d recorded output writes supported CXSMILES groups with readback verification.

requirements.summary: Requests are typed and versioned, with explicit compatibility and structured errors.

parts.summary: Errors use one v1 envelope with a stable code and, where relevant, current_revision and command_index.

Within one process and its replay window (the latest 64 successful mutations of an open document; keyed per document for edits, saves, autosaves and renames, per process for creates, closes, recoveries, draft discards, copies, deletes and restores), a repeated request_id with the same body returns the first reply without acting again, and reusing it for a different body is refused. A restart forgets every request_id.
The capability list reports features that are not implemented as not_implemented.

Operation contract 1: each request names its contract version, request_id, compatibility profile and operation; each reply gives an envelope, an outcome (ok, partial, error, unsupported), the document revision, a typed result, model_id, diagnostics with paths and details, and a loss report. HTTP and the CLI pass the request bytes to the same Application::execute, and failures carry the v1 error codes. The catalog states, per operation and per transaction sub-operation, representation apart from execution, with the follow-up for what does not run; an operation that does not run (every chem.* operation among them) is answered unsupported, never with a result. model_id is always null and the loss report always empty: no operation uses a model or drops content.

chem.aromaticity_convert computes outside the session lock on a copy of the graph, under a time limit (default 5 s, at most 8 s, set per request by time_limit_ms); a stopped computation is the time_limit diagnostic (or cancelled when its host cancels it), changes nothing, and is not remembered for replay (a stop is honoured until the result is committed under the lock, and the requested time_limit_ms is part of the replay comparison once a request has completed); a result computed for a revision that is no longer current is refused with revision_conflict. A time-based refusal depends on the machine; time_limit carries only limit_ms. Other operations have no time limit or cancel yet.

Model identifiers from operations that use a model or method, resource errors and cancel for operations other than the aromaticity conversion, reproducing observed behaviour under the legacy-observed profile, other adapters.
